sentences.text: 2  This MFA coming on for admission this day, the court delivered the following:
JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1), of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant - insurance company, challenging the judgment and award dated 06.01.2015, passed in MVC No.48/2013, on the file of Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Madikeri (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity), challenging the quantum of compensation.
2. Brief facts:
On 09.03.2012, at about 12.00 p.m. the claimant was going from Yadoor to Somwarpet by riding motor cycle bearing No. KA-12-H-2125.

When he reached Kalkandoor Junction on the road running from Somwarpet to Shanthalli, the rider of motor cycle bearing No. KA-55- H-3518 ridden in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the motor cycle of the claimant.
As a result, the claimant fell down and sustained injuries.
First he was shifted to the nearest government hospital at Somwarpet and thereafter he was admitted to Apollo Hospital, Mysuru, for higher treatment.
The claimant was an inpatient for 6 days in the hospital.
3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the claimant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Rs.8,77,010/- along with interest at 9% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Tribunal held the appellant - insurance company, liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials on record.
5.

The Tribunal has granted compensation under various heads as follows:
 a) Towards pain and Rs. 25,000.00  sufferings  b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 1,17,042.00  C) Towards loss of income Rs. 14,000.00  during laid -up period  d) Towards loss of future Rs. 6,25,968.00  income due to permanent  disability  e) Towards future Rs. 20,000.00  unhappiness  f) Towards attendant Rs. 15,000.00  charges,traveling expenses  and extra-nourishment  g)Towards future medical Rs. 60,000.00

sentences.text:
From the medical evidence on record including the doctors evidence, it is proved that the claimant had suffered the following injuries : -
1. Fracture shaft right femur 2. Left condyle fracture 3.
Right parasymphysis of mandible fracture 7.
The claimant was aged 23 years on the date of accident and had suffered the fractures stated above.

Award of compensation under the heads pain and sufferings, medical expenses, loss of income during laid-up period, future unhappiness, attendant charges, traveling expenses and extra-nourishment and future medical expenses are found to be proper and correct.
Therefore, on these heads the compensation awarded is not disturbed.
8. The Tribunal taking the notional income at Rs.7,000/- per month is found to be correct considering the year of accident.
It is in consonance with the notional income recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The doctor-CW1 has stated that the claimant has suffered 21% disability and CW2 has deposed that the claimant sustained disability of 15%.
Both the doctors have not stated whether the physical disability is in respect of the particular limbs or towards whole body.
Further more, the doctors have not stated whether it is a permanent partial disablement or permanent total disablement.
The Tribunal has applied the formula of A + B (90-A) and came to conclusion that the disability sustained is 27.6%.
The said formula is applicable in respect of assessment of a physical disability.
The parameters of assessment of function disability is different.
Doctors can only say physical disability.
The criteria for assessing functional disability is laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another [(2011) 1 SCC 343].

entities.text: Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another [(2011) 1 SCC 343]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The doctors have not stated whether the disability is with respect to the particular limbs or the whole body.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries sustained and the disability assessed by CWs 1 and 2 and the avocation of the claimant, i.e., doing furniture and electrical business, the functional disability can be taken at 20%.

9. This Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Ltd., Vs. Abdul & Others [MFA.NO.103807/2016 C/W MFA.NOS.103835/2016 & 103807/2018 DD.27.05.2022], has held that where there is severe disability affecting the future prospects in life, additional income has to be added.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd., Vs. Abdul & Others [MFA.NO.103807/2016 C/W MFA.NOS.103835/2016 & 103807/2018 DD.27.05.2022]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the age of the claimant as 23 years old, following the judgment of the Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680], 40% income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicable multiplier is '18'.

Therefore, loss of future income due to disability including future prospects in life is re-assessed and quantified as The Branch Manager, United India ... vs H N Karthik on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131273802/

sentences.text:
4 follows:
Rs.7,000/- + Rs.2,800/- (40% of Rs.7000)=Rs.9,800/-. Rs.9,800/- x 20% x 18 x 12 = Rs.4,23,360/- Accordingly, Rs.4,23,360/- is awarded under the head 'loss of future income due to disability including loss of future prospects in life'.
10.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads are found to be correct and they are not disturbed.

11. Thus, in all the claimant is entitled to compensation as under : -
 a) Towards pain and Rs. 25,000.00  sufferings  b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 1,17,042.00  C) Towards loss of income Rs. 14,000.00  during laid -up period  d) Towards loss of future Rs. 4,23,360.00  income due to permanent  disability  e) Towards future Rs. 20,000.00  unhappiness  f) Towards attendant Rs. 15,000.00  charges, traveling expenses  and extra-nourishment  g)Towards future medical Rs. 60,000.00  expenses  Total Rs. 6,74,402,.00 12.
The Tribunal has ordered interest at 9% from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The same is scaled down to 6% p.a.
Therefore, the above said compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
The other terms of the Tribunal are confirmed.
Hence the appeal filed by - 10 - the insurance company is liable to be allowed in part.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The judgment and award dated 06.01.2015, passed in MVC No.48/2013, on the file of Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Madikeri, is modified to an extent that the appellant - claimant is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.6,74,402/- instead of Rs.8,77,010/- along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till deposit.

iii. The amount in deposit shall be transferred to the Tribunal The Branch Manager, United India ... vs H N Karthik on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131273802/
5 forthwith.
